# SDLC Documentation — CloudTrail Security Insights

**Audience + purpose:** an index for the full SDLC documentation set, generated by exhaustively scanning the codebase (reading full files, citing `file:line`) and then adversarially verifying every load-bearing claim against the source. Written for **new engineers** and **open-source contributors**.

> Generated 2026-06-24, updated 2026-07-27 after security remediation pass (SQL-01, SUPPLY-01, ERR-01, TRUTH-01, REL-01, DATA-01). All docs were authored from an exhaustive code survey and cross-verified against the cited source. The security and test-coverage docs (09, 10) have been updated to reflect the remediation changes.

## The documents

| # | Doc | What it covers |
|---|-----|----------------|
| 01 | [01-REQUIREMENTS.md](01-REQUIREMENTS.md) | Functional (FR-*), non-functional (NFR-*), and security (SEC-*) requirements reverse-engineered from the code, with a traceability matrix to `file:line`. |
| 02 | [02-USER-STORIES.md](02-USER-STORIES.md) | Personas + "As a … I want … so that …" stories grouped by epic, each marked Built / Partial / Backlog. |
| 03 | [03-USER-JOURNEYS.md](03-USER-JOURNEYS.md) | End-to-end journeys (setup → creds → sync → index → query → investigate) with Mermaid sequence diagrams. |
| 04 | [04-HIGH-LEVEL-DESIGN.md](04-HIGH-LEVEL-DESIGN.md) | C4-ish system context, container, and deployment views; the single-binary `go:embed` model; SQLite vs DuckDB split. |
| 05 | [05-LOW-LEVEL-DESIGN.md](05-LOW-LEVEL-DESIGN.md) | Per-package internals, the handler→service→models contract, and "how to add an investigate scenario / LLM provider" walkthroughs. |
| 06 | [06-DATA-FLOW.md](06-DATA-FLOW.md) | Data path from S3 CloudTrail logs → extract → DuckDB index → query/rewrite → results; and prompt → Bedrock → SQL → DuckDB. Schema mapping. |
| 07 | [07-API-FLOW.md](07-API-FLOW.md) | APIs the system **calls** (S3, Bedrock, STS, Organizations) and the HTTP routes it **exposes**, with sequence diagrams. |
| 08 | [08-TECH-STACK.md](08-TECH-STACK.md) | Versioned technology matrix (layer × tech × version × why), cited to `go.mod` / `web/package.json`. |
| 09 | [09-TEST-COVERAGE.md](09-TEST-COVERAGE.md) | Honest per-package coverage table (real `go test -cover` numbers), why each low number is low, and prioritized test gaps. |
| 10 | [10-SECURITY.md](10-SECURITY.md) | As-built security posture, auth methods, trust boundaries, the SafeSQL allowlist. Links to the live review for open findings. |

Supporting file: [`.ground-truth.md`](.ground-truth.md) — frozen real counts, coverage numbers, route list, and dependencies used as the shared fact base.

## Start here (reading order by audience)

**New engineer (onboarding):**
1. [04-HIGH-LEVEL-DESIGN.md](04-HIGH-LEVEL-DESIGN.md) — the big picture
2. [03-USER-JOURNEYS.md](03-USER-JOURNEYS.md) — what the tool actually does, end to end
3. [08-TECH-STACK.md](08-TECH-STACK.md) — what it's built with
4. [05-LOW-LEVEL-DESIGN.md](05-LOW-LEVEL-DESIGN.md) — package internals + how to extend
5. [06-DATA-FLOW.md](06-DATA-FLOW.md) / [07-API-FLOW.md](07-API-FLOW.md) — how data and requests move

**Open-source contributor (adding a feature):**
1. [05-LOW-LEVEL-DESIGN.md](05-LOW-LEVEL-DESIGN.md) — the extension walkthroughs
2. [07-API-FLOW.md](07-API-FLOW.md) — the route + handler contract
3. [09-TEST-COVERAGE.md](09-TEST-COVERAGE.md) — where tests are missing (good first contributions)
4. [10-SECURITY.md](10-SECURITY.md) — the trust boundaries to respect
5. [01-REQUIREMENTS.md](01-REQUIREMENTS.md) / [02-USER-STORIES.md](02-USER-STORIES.md) — Built vs Backlog

## Verification status

Every doc was cross-verified against the cited code. Verdicts (all **minor-fixes**, none needs-rework):

| Doc | Verdict | Claims checked | Corrections applied |
|-----|---------|---------------:|--------------------:|
| 01-REQUIREMENTS | minor-fixes | 71 | 20 |
| 02-USER-STORIES | minor-fixes | 62 | 9 |

Corrections were mostly stale counts (e.g. investigate scenarios 28→40, prompt templates 47→38), broken sibling cross-links repointed to real filenames, line-citation precision, and softening of absolute language. Coverage percentages and scanner numbers were taken from the frozen `.ground-truth.md` rather than re-run during verification — re-run `go test -cover ./...` if you need them fresh.

### Honest note: one stale CODE comment (not a doc error)
The verifiers flagged that `cmd/analyzer/main.go:330-333` has a comment describing a "generous but capped" `WriteTimeout`, while the actual value is `WriteTimeout: 0` (disabled, for SSE). The docs correctly state it is `0`; the **code comment** is stale. Per the docs-only scope, no code was changed — this is left for a code owner. (Similarly, `internal/features/prompts/system_prompt.go` still references `kiro-cli`, which the docs correctly avoid.)
